g.text: FreeIPA Diagnosis
Host: ipa01.example.test Generated: 2026-09-16T04:48:47Z
Overall:
CRITICAL
PRIMARY PROBLEM
named failed to start: missing LDAP ACI for the DNS service principal
WHY
named/bind-dyndb-ldap logged an LDAP permission-denied error while starting up. This matches the
documented failure mode where ACIs for the DNS/<fqdn>@REALM principal under cn=dns are missing or
incorrect - most commonly after an LDIF restore or an upgrade that didn't reapply DNS ACIs. Without
those ACIs, bind-dyndb-ldap cannot read the DNS zone data it needs to start named.
EVIDENCE
✓ journal shows named/bind-dyndb-ldap failed to start with a permission/ACI error
✓ journal shows named/bind-dyndb-ldap crashing or failing to start
✓ journal shows named/bind-dyndb-ldap crashing or failing to start
✓ service health check reports named is not running
IMPACT
named is down: all DNS resolution this server is authoritative for (SRV/A/AAAA lookups clients depend on
for Kerberos and LDAP discovery) fails for clients pointed at this server.
DO THIS FIRST
Confirm the DNS service ACIs under cn=dns,<suffix> for the DNS/<fqdn>@REALM principal are actually
missing before changing anything
ldapsearch -Y GSSAPI -b 'cn=dns,$(ipa env basedn -o tsv 2>/dev/null || echo dc=example,dc=test)' aci
Safety:
SAFE — read-only, no state change.
2 additional step(s) - see --details.
ADDITIONAL ACTIONS
- Restore the standard DNS ACIs (compare against a known-good IPA DNS server, or reapply via the DNS
update LDIF shipped with ipa-server-dns)
Safety:
CAUTION — changes state, but is reversible and scoped.
- Restart named-pkcs11 once the ACIs are confirmed restored
systemctl restart named-pkcs11
Safety:
CAUTION — changes state, but is reversible and scoped.
CONFIDENCE
HIGH: [HIGH: freeipa.org/page/Troubleshooting/DNS + bind-dyndb-ldap's 'NamedCannotStart' doc] the
journal shows the specific LDAP permission-denied signature this failure mode is documented to produce,
not just a generic crash.
LIMITATIONS
Diagnosis is based on text pattern matching for the documented ACI-permission-denied signature; if
bind-dyndb-ldap's exact wording differs across versions, confirm by reading the full journal excerpt
manually before applying the ACI fix.
VERIFY
After addressing this, confirm with:
sudo ipa-diagnose verify
- named-pkcs11 is active and no longer logs the ACI/permission-denied error on startup
OTHER INDEPENDENT PROBLEMS
Not caused by the problem above - each needs its own investigation.
INDEPENDENT PROBLEM
DNS record(s) required for Kerberos/LDAP autodiscovery are broken
WHY
IPADNSSystemRecordsCheck reported ERROR (SRV record _ldap._tcp.example.test. required for LDAP
autodiscovery could not be resolved), and an independent live `dig` lookup confirms the affected record
is actually missing or resolving incorrectly.
EVIDENCE
✓ IPADNSSystemRecordsCheck flagged a system DNS record
✓ live dig lookup independently confirms this record is missing or wrong
✓ live dig lookup independently confirms this record is missing or wrong
✓ live dig lookup independently confirms this record is missing or wrong
IMPACT
Clients may fail Kerberos/LDAP server autodiscovery (SRV lookups) or CA chain retrieval (ipa-ca A/AAAA),
causing authentication or enrollment failures.
DO THIS FIRST
Diff live DNS records against the expected IPA system records
ipa dns-update-system-records --dry-run
Safety:
SAFE — read-only, no state change.
1 additional step(s) - see --details.
ADDITIONAL ACTIONS
- Add or correct the specific record identified above
ipa dnsrecord-add <zone> <name> --srv-rec='<priority> <weight> <port> <target>' # or
--a-rec/--aaaa-rec as appropriate
Safety:
CAUTION — changes state, but is reversible and scoped.
CONFIDENCE
HIGH: [HIGH: Red Hat 'Checking DNS records using IdM Healthcheck'] ERROR-level healthcheck result
corroborated by an independent live dig lookup showing the same record is broken.
LIMITATIONS
ipahealthcheck's IPADNSSystemRecordsCheck (and this pack's own dns_lookup collector) only resolve
against resolver(s) reachable from this one host. In a multi-server IPA DNS topology, a clean result
here does not confirm every IPA DNS server serves correct records - freeipa.org's DNS troubleshooting
page documents this as a known blind spot. Spot-check `dig` against every known IPA DNS server before
considering DNS fully verified. If the original symptom was a downstream Kerberos discovery failure,
re-run the kerberos pack's checks after this fix for true end-to-end verification.
VERIFY
After addressing this, confirm with:
sudo ipa-diagnose verify
- Re-run IPADNSSystemRecordsCheck for SUCCESS and re-confirm via a fresh dig that the record now
resolves correctly
RELATED SYMPTOMS
• Kerberos authentication failing because no KDC could be found or reached
(related to: named failed
to start: missing LDAP ACI for the DNS service principal, DNS record(s) required for Kerberos/LDAP
autodiscovery are broken)
kinit failed because no KDC could be contacted for the realm, with no clock-skew or KVNO-mismatch
evidence present to explain the failure instead. The most commonly documented root cause for this
pattern is missing or incorrect DNS SRV records for the Kerberos realm.
Diagnostic packs evaluated: directory-server, dns, kerberos, replication, certificates
